thread:
support-agent: FYI customer reported intermittent 400/404 when calling tools after a rename. Happens ~10% of calls, mostly from EU region. Customer says it started after yesterday's rename rollout.
ryan: Can you paste the raw API error and request body? 400 vs 404 are different failures.
support-agent: Customer sent this error payload: `{"error":"tool_not_found","detail":"could not find tool 'InvoiceGenV2'"}`. Their client is calling `InvoiceGenV2` (capital V2). The old name was `invoice-gen-v2`.
anna.k: Are they on a private deployment or hosted API?
support-agent: Hosted API (prod). Tenant id: t-8342. Example request (sanitized): ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \
-H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
-d '{"tool":"InvoiceGenV2","args":{"invoice_id":12345}}'``` They say retrying sometimes returns success.
liam: OK this looks like a casing/alias issue. Registry canonical names are lowercase `invoice-gen-v2`. We have alias mapping that should handle renamed handles. Could be a cache TTL on edge clients or an old model router not seeing alias. @deploy-bot any recent rollout touching registry-sync?
deploy-bot: Deployment: service/registry-sync v3.2.1 deployed 2026-02-18T10:22:41Z to prod (EU). Rollout status: 100%.
sre-oncall: I’ll tail the registry sync logs for t-8342. Can you reproduce with a curl that includes X-Request-Id so we can trace?
ryan: I just tried caller with `InvoiceGenV2` and got `404 tool not found`. Then retried immediately and got 200. Captured two request ids: req_eu_0001 (404) and req_eu_0002 (200). Logs:
```
[10:34:12Z] req_eu_0001 router.lookup tool=InvoiceGenV2 -> NOT_FOUND cache_miss
[10:34:12Z] req_eu_0001 registry.query alias_lookup=InvoiceGenV2 -> not found
[10:34:13Z] req_eu_0002 router.lookup tool=InvoiceGenV2 -> FOUND invoice-gen-v2 via alias
[10:34:13Z] req_eu_0002 proxy.forward -> 200
```
support-agent: So first request missed alias, second hit after registry warmed. Customer sees this intermittently which is bad.
anna.k: Could be a race during registry rollout where some router instances have older alias maps. Edge caches may TTL after config push. What’s the alias propagation mechanism? Is it pub/sub + per-instance update?
liam: Yes, registry-sync publishes diffs to the config bus and instances subscribe. There’s also an in-memory alias cache with 30s TTL. If an instance misses a diff (network blip) it falls back to local cache until TTL expires. If alias was created and older instances didn't get it, they return NOT_FOUND until they fetch on miss.
sre-oncall: For t-8342 I see intermittent transient 503s to config-bus around 10:21Z that caused ~12 instances to miss the push for ~40s. That matches the timeframe.
ryan: Repro steps I used: 1) run 10 parallel curl calls with `tool=InvoiceGenV2` 2) observe ~15% 404s on first wave, then subsequent waves OK. Attached captured request ids.
support-agent: Customer is asking for a mitigation and whether we can do a backfill so their clients don't see errors.
liam: Short term: we can increase alias cache TTL to 0 (always hit registry) or implement a synchronous lookup on cache miss (costly). Long term: add handshake retry for config updates and a temporary sticky fallback that tries a registry lookup on NOT_FOUND before returning to client.
anna.k: For this customer we should enable immediate registry fallback for their tenant. We can add a feature flag on router: `force_registry_lookup_on_not_found: true` per-tenant.
sre-oncall: I can apply a per-tenant flag for t-8342 on the routing layer. Will flip it and monitor errors.
liam: Also run a one-time backfill to populate alias into all routers: `POST /internal/routers/backfill?t=t-8342&alias=InvoiceGenV2` (internal only). That should reduce the hit rate while the config bus fix is being rolled out.
ryan: I ran the backfill and immediately saw the 404 rate drop to 0 in my small test.
support-agent: Great. Customer wants ETA and permanent fix.
liam: ETA: apply per-tenant fallback now (minutes). Schedule: patch to registry-sync to add delivery ACKs and retries next week, plus increase cache coherence test coverage. I'll open an eng-runtime ticket and tag oncall.
support-agent: Noted. I'll message the customer with the temporary mitigation and ETA. Any postmortem items we should capture?
anna.k: Capture: 1) config-bus transient failures 2) lack of synchronous fallback on NOT_FOUND 3) monitoring gap — alert if alias create doesn't reach >95% of routers within 30s. 4) clarify casing/normalization docs for clients.
liam: Also add a regression test for rename rollouts under partial bus failure.
sre-oncall: I’ll keep monitoring t-8342 for 1 hour and follow up. If anyone sees a spike, ping me.
support-agent: Thanks all — I'll update the ticket and tell the customer we've applied the workaround and are working on a permanent fix. :thumbsup:
